issue_title: P1: Revisão geral de code patterns, código repetido e performance
scope: General codebase review across apps/, libs/, services/, packages/ for patterns consistency, code duplication, performance bottlenecks, security, error handling, and test coverage

design_decisions.decision: Review will be organized by architectural layer: apps (frontend), libs (shared Python libraries), services (backend APIs), packages (npm packages)
design_decisions.rationale: The monorepo has clear separation of concerns; reviewing by layer allows systematic coverage and clear ownership

design_decisions.decision: Focus on 6 dimensions per the issue scope: code patterns, duplicated code, performance, security, error handling, tests
design_decisions.rationale: Matches the explicit checklist in the issue body and ensures comprehensive coverage

design_decisions.decision: Output consolidated report at docs/reports/code-review-geral.md with per-service checklists, priority (P0/P1/P2), and fix suggestions with examples
design_decisions.rationale: Explicitly required by the issue deliverable; makes findings actionable for downstream remediation tasks

design_decisions.decision: Leverage existing documentation (patterns.md, repo-index.md, agent_audits/, SHARED_MEMORY_DESIGN.md) as baseline for expected patterns
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids re-discovering known patterns; ensures review validates against documented standards

design_decisions.decision: Use automated tooling where possible: grep/rg for pattern detection, pyright/mypy for Python type consistency, eslint for TS, dependency analysis for duplication
design_decisions.rationale: Codebase is large (~17k files); manual-only review is impractical. Automation finds systematic issues efficiently

design_decisions.decision: Prioritize findings by impact: P0 = security/data-loss/blocking bugs, P1 = performance/maintainability, P2 = style/minor inconsistency
design_decisions.rationale: Issue is P1 but findings will vary; clear prioritization guides remediation sequencing

subtasks.title: Inventory & baseline: catalog all services/libs with primary language, entry points, and known patterns
subtasks.description: Scan apps/, libs/, services/, packages/ to build a service catalog. Document each: primary language, main entry points, key dependencies, and reference patterns from patterns.md/SHARED_MEMORY_DESIGN.md

subtasks.title: Code patterns consistency review
subtasks.description: Check naming conventions (files, functions, variables), import/export patterns, project structure, type safety (pyright/mypy for Python, eslint/tsc for TS), error handling patterns, logging patterns, config management patterns across all layers

subtasks.title: Code duplication detection & shared lib extraction candidates
subtasks.description: Find duplicated logic across libs/ (e.g., validation, DB access, auth, serialization), services/ (common middleware, error handlers), and apps/ (hooks, utils). Identify candidates for extraction to blu_shared_utils or new shared libs. Use jscpd/duplication detection tools

subtasks.title: Performance bottleneck analysis
subtasks.description: Identify N+1 queries (Supabase/Postgres), unbatched API calls, excessive allocations in hot paths, missing indexes, inefficient loops, missing caching, async/await misuse, large bundle sizes in apps/blu_v3

subtasks.title: Security review
subtasks.description: Check input validation/sanitization (Zod/Pydantic), SQL injection risks (raw SQL vs ORM/rpc), auth/authorization consistency (blu_auth usage), rate limiting, secrets management (.env, .secrets.baseline), CORS, CSP headers, dependency vulnerabilities (npm audit, pip-audit)

subtasks.title: Error handling consistency
subtasks.description: Verify error types hierarchy, user-facing vs internal errors, logging with context, retry policies, circuit breakers, dead letter handling, error boundary patterns in frontend, correlation IDs for tracing

subtasks.title: Test coverage & quality assessment
subtasks.description: Measure coverage per service (pytest-cov, jest --coverage), identify missing edge cases, mock quality, fixture reusability, integration vs unit balance, test organization, flaky test detection

subtasks.title: Consolidate findings into docs/reports/code-review-geral.md
subtasks.description: Generate the required deliverable: per-service checklist, P0/P1/P2 priority for each finding, fix suggestions with code examples, remediation effort estimates, and cross-cutting themes

risks.risk: Codebase size (~17k files including node_modules) makes manual review infeasible
risks.mitigation: Heavy reliance on automated tooling (grep, linters, duplication detectors); sampling for deep-dive

risks.risk: Some patterns may be intentional deviations (e.g., service-specific conventions)
risks.mitigation: Flag as 'review needed' rather than 'violation'; consult service owners via comments

risks.risk: Depends on completion of Phases 1-5 (#17-#37) - reviewing prematurely may miss new code
risks.mitigation: This intake documents the plan; execution should wait for dependency completion signal

risks.risk: TypeScript and Python ecosystems have different tooling; unified reporting needs normalization
risks.mitigation: Standardize finding schema: {file, line, layer, dimension, severity, description, suggestion, example}

design_questions.question: Should the review include generated/build artifacts (e.g., libs/blu_context_service/build/)?
design_questions.recommendation: Exclude build/ and node_modules/; focus on source only

design_questions.question: What is the target remediation timeline? This affects P0/P1/P2 thresholds
design_questions.recommendation: Default to: P0=immediate, P1=next sprint, P2=tech debt backlog

design_questions.question: Are there specific services/libs that are higher priority (e.g., agent_api, blu_agent_framework)?
design_questions.recommendation: Weight findings by service criticality; core framework libs get stricter thresholds
